surface_mechanism_description: NH3 plasma interacts with the Ru~EtCp)2 precursor, weakening the Ru-~EtCp! bond and activating the reducing reaction by forming volatile compounds with the ligands in Ru~EtCp)2. The absence of secondary adsorption in PEALD reduces the number of Ru~EtCp)2 molecules consumed per cycle, leading to a thinner film thickness/cycle.
intermediate_species: volatile compounds from ligands in Ru~EtCp)2
evidence: The lone pair of electrons in the NH3 interacts with the ruthenium in the Ru~EtCp)2 and weakens the Ru-~EtCp! bond, and that the excited species in NH3 plasma activate the reducing reaction by making volatile compounds with the ligands in Ru~EtCp)2. These results show that NH3 plasma successfully reduces the metal-organic precursor of Ru~EtCp)2 into elementary ruthenium.
